annotations.title: What changed in these records since a date

description: Resuming work on facts you read from us earlier? This answers "what moved since <date>" in one call. Returns each record whose values changed on or after that date, newest first, with the record's url, the field that moved and the before and after values where we hold them, plus the verbatim source passage and page for the ones we have written up. Use it instead of re-reading a whole dataset or polling a feed per dataset. Only the 156 datasets that publish a change history can answer: the reply always names the ones it read, so an empty answer means "nothing changed in these", never "nothing changed anywhere". One call reads the most recently changed histories; pass dataset_slug for one dataset, which is complete for that dataset. POLLING ON A SCHEDULE? Every reply carries a `cursor`: pass it back next time instead of a date and you get only what has moved since that call, with nothing repeated and nothing skipped — which a date cannot do, because the finest grain we record is a day. The reply also separates the datasets we have been back to since your date from the ones we have NOT looked at, because their silence means different things.

cursor.description: The `cursor` string from a previous reply. Resumes exactly after the last row you were given: no repeats, nothing skipped, and a truncated answer is finished by calling again with the new cursor. Replaces `since`. Keep one cursor per scope — a whole-portfolio cursor is refused on a dataset_slug call rather than quietly answering a different question. The reply says whether the cursor moved and, when it did not, why.

dataset_slug.description: Optional. One dataset's change history instead of the most recently changed ones — cheaper, and complete for that dataset. Any dataset that publishes a change history: they are listed, with the date each last moved, at /change-feeds.json.

limit.description: Most changed records to return, 1 to 200. Default 50. The reply says how many were left off, and with a cursor the next call finishes them.

since.description: ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD. Changes detected on or after this day are returned. Use the day you last read us. Required on a first call; afterwards send `cursor` instead.

name: changed_since
